## Initial stable release

First public release of the JDownloader 2 Docker image for Unraid — built on
top of LinuxServer's KasmVNC base image, with a dark interface ready out of
the box and zero manual first-run configuration.

## What it does

- **JDownloader 2** — full GUI in your browser, no VNC client, no manual JAR
  setup. Container auto-downloads and installs JDownloader on first start.
- **KasmVNC web frontend** — hardware-accelerated rendering, real browser
  clipboard, native file upload and download.
- **Modern dark interface** — pre-applied JD Plain Dark theme with the KDE
  Breeze Dark colour palette. Switch to light with `JD_THEME=Light`.
- **Java 21 JRE** with full AWT/Swing support (not headless).
- **Multi-arch** — `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`.
- **Update-safe config** — `/config` survives every `docker pull`.

## Dark-theme integration (under the hood)

JDownloader's default Swing renderer is not designed for dark themes. This
image bundles several layers that make `FLATLAF_DARK` actually look right:

- **Pre-patched FlatLaf 3.7 JAR** with explicit Breeze Dark overrides for
  every relevant Swing component (`Table.background`, `List.background`,
  `Panel.background`, `Viewport.background`, etc.) baked into
  `FlatDarkLaf.properties`.
- **Pre-seeded `flatlaf.dep.json`** so JD's AWU registry treats FlatLaf as
  already installed — no install dialog on first start.
- **JVM agent** (`jd-dark-agent.jar`) loaded via `-javaagent` that:
  - Pushes UIManager colours after JD's LAF initialization
  - Dismisses the "Tray isn't supported" error dialog
  - Accepts the "Design-Update" dialog (registers FLATLAF_DARK)
  - Accepts the "Erweiterungen verwalten" / "Manage Extensions" prompt
- **Pre-seeded JD theme files** for `JD_Plain_Dark` and `FLATLAF_DARK`.

## Known limitation

JDownloader's custom download list / link grabber renderer (`ExtTable`) caches
its background colour at component-creation time and does not re-read
`UIManager.getColor("Table.background")` after the LAF is applied. The result
is that the menu bar, toolbar, tab headers and scrollbars correctly switch to
dark colours, but the **download list and link grabber content area keep a
white background**.

This is a JD-side renderer issue that cannot be fixed from outside the
JDownloader codebase. A bug report has been submitted upstream.

Everything else — chrome, menus, dialogs, toolbar — renders dark as designed.

## Configuration

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `JD_THEME` | `Dark` | `Dark` = JD Plain Dark (Breeze Dark), `Light` = JD Plain |
| `PUID` / `PGID` | `99` / `100` | User/Group ID (Unraid: nobody/users) |
| `TZ` | `Europe/Vienna` | Timezone |
| `CUSTOM_USER` | _(empty)_ | KasmVNC username — empty = no auth |
| `PASSWORD` | _(empty)_ | KasmVNC password |
| `TITLE` | `JDownloader 2` | Browser tab title |
| `UMASK` | `022` | File-creation mask |

| Port | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `3000` | KasmVNC HTTP |
| `3001` | KasmVNC HTTPS (self-signed) |

| Volume | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `/config` | Persistent JD install, configs, sessions |
| `/downloads` | Download destination |

## Installation

Unraid template: drop the XML into `/boot/config/plugins/dockerMan/templates-user/`
with the filename **`my-JDownloader.xml`** (capital J, `my-` prefix — otherwise
dockerMan will conflict with Unraid's own naming and force-updates will reset
your settings). One-liner:

```bash
wget -O /boot/config/plugins/dockerMan/templates-user/my-JDownloader.xml \
    https://raw.githubusercontent.com/junkerderprovinz/jdownloader/main/templates/jdownloader.xml
```

docker-compose users: see the example in [README](../../README.md#docker-compose-non-unraid).
